highlightAliases.old: Assess rehab potential only after acute illness resolves — delirium, hemodynamic instability, occult fracture, acute infection delay it (p821).
highlightAliases.new: Assess rehab potential after acute illness resolves — delirium, hemodynamic instability, occult fracture, acute infection may delay referral to rehabilitation (p821).

highlightAliases.old: Flexibility: 90 degrees knee flexion for stairs; 120 to 150 degrees shoulder flexion/abduction to reach overhead (p825).
highlightAliases.new: Flexibility: at least 90 degrees knee flexion for stairs; 120 to 150 degrees shoulder flexion/abduction to reach overhead (p825).

highlightAliases.old: Cardiac rehab: only one-third of eligible patients participate (12% in a 600k-patient Medicare cohort) (p830). CR vs. none: mortality 2.3% vs. 5.3%; benefit sustained at 5 years, 16% vs. 25% (p830). ≥25 sessions → 20% lower 5-yr mortality vs. fewer sessions (p830). Heart failure: stable 3 to 4 weeks before starting; CR → 28% lower mortality/hospitalization, 29% lower death rate, peak VO2 +15% to 30%, symptoms/ADLs/well-being +15% to 50%; QoL gains seen as early as 2 months (p830).
highlightAliases.new: Cardiac rehab: only one-third of eligible patients participate (12% in a cohort of more than 600,000 Medicare patients) (p830). CR vs. none: mortality 2.3% vs. 5.3%; benefit sustained at 5 years, 16% vs. 25% (p830). ≥25 sessions → 20% lower 5-yr mortality vs. fewer sessions (p830). Heart failure: stable at least 3 to 4 weeks before starting; CR → 28% lower mortality/hospitalization, 29% lower death rate, peak VO2 +15% to 30%, symptoms/ADLs/well-being +15% to 50%; QoL gains seen as early as 2 months (p830).

highlightAliases.old: Stroke: rehab can begin as early as 24 to 48 hours poststroke once the patient is medically stable (p831). Dysphagia silent in up to one-third; aphasia in one-third (p831). highlightAliases.new: Stroke: rehab can begin as early as 24 to 48 hours poststroke once the patient is medically stable (p831). highlightAliases.old: Post-THA (posterolateral): avoid >90 degrees hip flexion early (p832).
highlightAliases.new: Post-THA (posterolateral): may need to avoid more than 90 degrees hip flexion early (p832).

highlightAliases.old: Diabetic foot disease: Medicare covers one pair of shoes/inserts each year (p829).
highlightAliases.new: Diabetes and severe diabetic foot disease: Medicare covers one pair of therapeutic shoes and inserts or shoe modifications each year (p829).

highlightAliases.old: Cardiac rehab: only one-third of eligible patients participate (12% in a 600k-patient Medicare cohort) (p830). Heart failure: stable at least 3 to 4 weeks before starting; CR → 28% lower mortality/hospitalization, 29% lower death rate, peak VO2 +15% to 30%, symptoms/ADLs/well-being +15% to 50%; QoL gains seen as early as 2 months (p830).
highlightAliases.new: Cardiac rehab: only one-third of eligible patients participate (12% in a cohort of more than 600,000 Medicare patients) (p830). CR vs. none: mortality 2.3% vs. 5.3%; benefit sustained at 5 years, 16% vs. 25% (p830). ≥25 sessions → 20% lower 5-yr mortality vs. fewer sessions (p830). Heart failure: stable at least 3 to 4 weeks before starting; CR → 28% lower mortality/hospitalization, 29% lower death rate, peak VO2 +15% to 30%, symptoms/ADLs/well-being +15% to 50%; QoL gains seen as early as 2 months (p830).

highlightAliases.old: Inpatient rehab facility: at least 3 hours of therapy/day required, 24-hr nursing (p822).
highlightAliases.new: US Medicare inpatient rehabilitation includes 24-hour rehabilitation nursing and generally 3 hours of therapy per day on at least 5 days/week, or 15 hours in 7 consecutive days in documented cases. Multiple therapy disciplines participate, including PT or OT (p822; CMS inpatient rehabilitation criteria).

highlightAliases.old: PAD: walk-to-pain program needs ≥6 months for benefit (p830).
highlightAliases.new: PAD with claudication: supervised exercise uses intermittent walking to moderate-to-maximum symptoms, alternating with rest. A standard program is 30–45 minutes of active exercise at least 3 times/week for at least 12 weeks; continue training thereafter. The six-month period described on p830 is not a minimum time to benefit (2024 ACC/AHA PAD guideline).

highlightAliases.old: An inpatient rehab facility requires a minimum of 3 hours of therapy daily; a skilled nursing facility has no required intensity or duration of therapy (p822).
highlightAliases.new: A US Medicare inpatient rehabilitation facility generally provides 3 hours of therapy on at least 5 days/week, or 15 hours over 7 consecutive days in documented cases. A skilled nursing facility has no equivalent fixed session-intensity requirement (p822, CMS inpatient rehabilitation coverage criteria).
